title: Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims: who may lodge a claim and how many claims a cover takes
content:
## Scope

This part of the notice and time bar policy of the Cargo Liability, CargoCare and Cargo Claims product line governs who may lodge a claim on a cover, how many claims a cover takes, and the withdrawal of an open claim.

## Policy clause

1. A claim is lodged by the claimant, which only the claimant can do, by written notice naming the container and the loss. Lodging moves the cover into the open-claim state, whether the cover was active or already in the closed-claim state after an earlier claim on the same shipment.
2. The claimant must be one the product admits: the cover holder, or the consignee named on the transport document where the product lists the named consignee among those who may lodge. A consignee is recognised only when its registered company name matches the consignee name printed on the transport document exactly.
3. A cover takes at most the product's maximum number of claims. The count covers the claims lodged on the cover over its life whose outcome is not withdrawn, leaving out the claim being handled.
4. Only one claim is open on a cover at a time.
5. The claimant may withdraw an open claim. Withdrawal returns the cover to active, and the withdrawn claim does not count toward the maximum.
6. A claim, once decided by settlement or rejection, is closed by the desk, which moves the cover from the open-claim state to the closed-claim state.

The entitlement and the count rest on the system records: the cover and its holder, the consignee name printed on the transport document, the claimant's registered company name, and the claim files on the cover.

## Entitlement check

| Claimant | Admitted when |
|---|---|
| The cover holder | Always among those the product may admit |
| The consignee named on the transport document | The product lists the named consignee, and the registered company name matches the printed consignee name exactly |
| Anyone else | Not admitted |

## Hypothetical cases

- **Case A (hypothetical names):** the transport document prints the consignee as "Baltic Reef Traders Oy", and the caller's registered company name is "Baltic Reef Traders Oy". The names match exactly, so the consignee is recognised where the product lists the named consignee.
- **Case B (hypothetical names):** the printed consignee is "Baltic Reef Traders Oy" and the registered company name is "Baltic Reef Traders". The names do not match exactly, so that customer is not recognised as the named consignee.
- **Case C (hypothetical cap of 4):** a cover shows three earlier claims, one of them withdrawn, and none open. The count is two, below the hypothetical maximum of 4, and no claim is open, so neither limit stands in the way of a new claim.

## Points of judgement

**The claimant withdrew a claim last month. Does it use up one of the allowed claims?** No. Withdrawn claims do not count toward the maximum.
